title: Transport an ordinary normalized Hom comparison to the one-point ring site
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings and φ:A→B. Let F and hF specify objects of scalar extension as in [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], and M,N be module sheaves on the one-object bottom-topology site. Put M₀=M(*) and N₀=N(*), with B an A-algebra via φ. Given any B-linear map k:B tensor_A Hom_A(M₀,N₀)→Hom_B(B tensor_A M₀,B tensor_A N₀) with k(b tensor f)(c tensor x)=bc tensor f(x), there is a sheaf morphism g:F(Hom_A(M,N))→Hom_B(F(M),F(N)) satisfying the same identity using ringExtensionPure at every U; IsIso g if and only if k is bijective. No finiteness, projectivity or flatness is assumed.

proof.text: Construct point_eq and slice_eq by eliminating the singleton objects. Construct pointLift by using the supplied linear map at every object; after substituting point_eq, every arrow is the identity and naturality is the presheaf identity law. Construct pointHomEquiv by evaluating at the identity slice object and taking the constant-component inverse. Substituting slice_eq proves naturality and both inverse identities; addition and scalar multiplication are componentwise.

Construct pointExtensionEquiv from the component of the module sheafification unit and eqToHom(hF(M).symm). The change-of-rings presheaf has value B tensor_A M(*). Presheaf.isSheaf_bot and isIso_toSheafify show its sheafification unit is invertible, so ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso gives the bijectivity required by LinearEquiv.ofBijective. The equality transport is likewise invertible. Their composite sends b tensor x to ringExtensionPure by definitional equality (pointExtensionEquiv_tmul).

Tensor pointHomEquiv M N using AlgebraTensorModule.congr, and compose with the inverse pointExtensionEquiv for internal Hom to obtain the source equivalence eS. Compose LinearEquiv.arrowCongr eM eN with the inverse B internal-Hom equivalence to obtain eT. Set l = eT composed with k composed with eS, and g = pointLift l. Prove pointLift_isIso_iff: evaluate an isomorphism for the forward implication; for the reverse implication lift the inverse LinearEquiv.ofBijective and verify both inverse equations at the unique object. Cancel the bijective eS and eT to get IsIso g iff k is bijective. Substitute point_eq for arbitrary U, rewrite pure tensors using pointExtensionEquiv_tmul, cancel the equivalences, and apply congrArg eN to hk.

theorem ringHomExtension_transport
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    (F : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules B)
    (hF : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap φ) M)
    (M N : RingSiteModules A) :
    letI := φ.toAlgebra
    ∀ (k : B ⊗[A] ((M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) →ₗ[A]
          (N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) →ₗ[B]
        ((B ⊗[A] (M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) →ₗ[B]
          (B ⊗[A] (N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)))))
      (hk : ∀ (b c : B)
        (f : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) →ₗ[A] N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
        (x : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)),
        k (b ⊗ₜ[A] f) (c ⊗ₜ[A] x) = (b * c) ⊗ₜ[A] f x),
    ∃ g : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) M N) ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf B) (F.obj M) (F.obj N),
      (IsIso g ↔ Function.Bijective k) ∧ ∀ (U : (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})ᵒᵖ) (b c : B)
        (f : (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) M N).val.obj U)
        (x : M.val.obj U),
        ((g.val.app U (ringExtensionPure φ F hF _ U b f)).app
          (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) (ringExtensionPure φ F hF M U c x) =
        ringExtensionPure φ F hF N U (b * c) ((f.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) x)
